items.headline: Tech bounces, bitcoin doesn't: BTC rejected near $83.1k as the Nasdaq rebounds
items.blurb: Monday's chip-led rebound clawed back part of the Nasdaq's worst week since June. Bitcoin poked above $83,000 early in Europe, was sold back within the hour and ended the US session near $81.8k — about 2% lower WoW and still below last week's ~$84k ceiling.
items.why_matters: BTC is lagging a risk-on bounce — a sign spot demand is thin; a close through ~$84k is the first sign equities are pulling crypto with them.

items.headline: October hike odds settle back near 16–20%; December hike still priced (Estimated)
items.blurb: CME FedWatch, as quoted by FXBus on 10-19, shows ~16% odds of a 25bp hike on Oct 28 vs ~84% hold; a ZQ-futures replica early 10-20 shows ~20%. A December hike is ~92% priced. Yesterday's ~65% quote was not confirmed by any other CME-citing source. FedWatch Advisors' Ben Emons argues October is underpriced.
items.why_matters: An October hold is the base case, so next week's FOMC is less of a cliff than Monday's outlier implied — but the path is still tightening, and Warsh's press conference is the swing event.

items.headline: 10-year yield climbs back to ~5.14% as bond desks brace for a hike
items.blurb: Treasury yields rose on Monday as traders priced energy-driven inflation; the 10-year ended near 5.135% and the 2-year near 4.76%. That is still slightly below a week ago but well above mid-September. The expiring November WTI contract settled at $103.66.
items.why_matters: Higher long yields and oil above $100 keep real-rate pressure on risk assets; the dollar is softer WoW but still up MoM.

items.headline: US issues security alerts across 12 Middle East locations; oil reverses early drop
items.blurb: The US warned citizens in 12 locations including Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iran and Israel of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures, stoking fears of fresh strikes on Iran and more Hormuz disruption. WTI bounced off its Asian-session low.
items.why_matters: Hormuz is still the main inflation wildcard — an oil spike feeds hike fears right before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs shed ~$910M in two weeks; Monday's early print is negative again
items.blurb: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost ~$228.6M in the week to Oct 16 after ~$681M the week before, leaving October about −$615M. Farside's Monday 10-19 row shows −$138.5M with IBIT not yet reported, so it is excluded until complete.
items.why_matters: ETF demand is still the weak link — outflows are slowing week on week but have not turned, which caps rallies.
